title: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia 2026 Manila Leg 3 Review: The Series' Biggest Field
seo_title: Trilogy Run Asia Manila Leg 3 2026 Review | SM MOA
meta_description: Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia 2026 Manila Leg 3 review: September 6 at SM Mall of Asia -- a flat course and the series' largest field, over 11,600 in 2025.
dek: Set for 6 September 2026 at SM Mall of Asia / Seaside Boulevard, this is the Manila leg finale of the Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia series -- a flat course that drew over 11,600 runners in its March 2025 opener, with the signature 32K distance on offer.
verdict: Manila Leg 3 closes out the Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia's progressive three-leg format with the signature 32K distance alongside 5K, 10K and 21K, on a course Runna classifies as flat -- set at SM Mall of Asia, the Philippines' largest shopping mall, on reclaimed land along Manila Bay. This is the series' biggest draw by field size: over 11,600 runners took part in the March 2025 Manila Leg 1 alone, about 5,000 of them in the 16K category. Multi-year continuity (formerly branded HOKA Trilogy Run Asia) suggests solid operational experience, even though independent participant reviews remain scarce.

sections.heading: A Flat Finale at SM Mall of Asia
paragraphs: The race is held at SM Mall of Asia / Seaside Boulevard in Pasay City, and Runna classifies the Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia course as flat. [1] SM Mall of Asia sits on reclaimed land along Manila Bay and is the largest shopping mall in the Philippines by floor area -- a venue built for large-scale events, which suits a race series of this size. [2]

sections.heading: The 32K Signature Distance
paragraphs: Manila Leg 3 2026 offers 5K, 10K, 21K and 32K distances, part of a progressive three-leg format per city that builds up in distance across the year before a National Finals in November. [1] That progression structure -- shorter distances early in the year, building to the 32K by Leg 3 -- mirrors the format used at the Iloilo and Cebu legs covered elsewhere in this series.

sections.heading: The Series' Biggest Field
paragraphs: The series draws genuinely large fields in Manila -- over 11,600 runners took part in the March 2025 Manila Leg 1, with about 5,000 in the 16K category alone. [1] The event is organised by Runrio (RUNRIO president Rio de la Cruz) with Santé Barley as title sponsor, and has run multi-year editions under different names, formerly branded HOKA Trilogy Run Asia -- continuity that suggests a mature, well-tested operation.

sections.heading: Early Cutoffs for Shorter Distances
paragraphs: A Pinoy Fitness forum commenter noted that fun-run distances like the 5K typically start very early, around 5am, with about a 1-hour cutoff for that category -- tight, but consistent with how RunRio manages Manila's heat and road-closure schedules for its shorter categories.

sections.heading: Reviews Are Still Thin
paragraphs: No independent participant race reports or reviews with course/organisation feedback were found for this specific Manila Leg 3 event or its recent predecessors -- most available coverage is organiser press releases and results-only news pool stories. [1] Listings on review aggregator sites such as Let's Do This currently show no submitted runner reviews for this event, despite its large field size.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're chasing the Trilogy series' National Finals qualification or simply want a flat, large-field race in one of Manila's most accessible venues, Manila Leg 3 on 6 September 2026 is a solid choice with real operational track record behind it, even if independent reviews haven't caught up to its scale yet.
